messages.content: Can you take a zero-downtime deploy pipeline?
Yes, taking a zero-downtime deploy pipeline.
Once the release settles, tightening the pod security admission profile is where attention goes.
The bulk of the diff sits in scripts/rollout.sh. If this breaks later we can roll back. After the spike, Velero for cluster backups was the clear winner.
Next steps for a zero-downtime deploy pipeline?
Thanks to the ingress with automatic certificate renewal, the on-call pages stopped. Resource requests and limits for all containers has been live since Tuesday with no complaints.
Nobody needs to think about node affinity rules keeping the databases separate anymore.
Spot instances for the batch workloads feels like the right fit here.
External-secrets backed by Vault is the direction we committed to. Horizontal pod autoscaling on CPU and request rate came off the board this morning. Fine by me.
The bulk of the diff sits in terraform/cluster.tf.
Thanks to a canary stage in the deploy pipeline, the on-call pages stopped. Nothing is waiting on anyone at the moment.
Next steps for a zero-downtime deploy pipeline?
A rolling deploy with surge and unavailable tuned held up fine through the whole load test.
